title: Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage Total Loss Manual
content:
## When a vehicle is a total loss

A vehicle insured under Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage is a total loss when the repair estimate total is at or above the policy state's total-loss threshold percentage of the actual cash value, or when a stolen vehicle is not recovered. Actual cash value comes from a valuation report of at least the minimum number of comparable vehicles within the comparable radius of the garaging ZIP (3 comparables within 150 miles on every deductible option).

## Payees and payment

- A loss payee is paid first, up to the loan or lease payoff on the payoff letter, and the rest goes to the insured.
- The settlement is paid only after the customer has accepted the settlement offer, and within the payment period (10 calendar days on every option) after the signed title (or owner-retained salvage paperwork) and the acceptance are received.
- A total-loss settlement is paid only when the settlement offer for that claim has been accepted by the customer. The offer status is read from the settlement record of that claim.
- Physical damage on the vehicle is removed once the settlement is paid.

## Unrecovered theft

An unrecovered stolen vehicle is settled only after the theft waiting period (30 calendar days on every option) has passed since the theft was reported. Days are counted from the report date of the theft claim, that date being day 0, and settlement is allowed from the last day of the waiting period onward.

| Theft reported | Settlement date | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Day 0 | Day 30 | Allowed |
| Day 0 | Day 29 | Not yet allowed |

A vehicle recovered after settlement belongs to Cardinal; the customer may buy it back within the buy-back period (30 calendar days on every option) of the recovery notice by returning the settlement less the vehicle's damage.

## Disputed value

A customer who disputes actual cash value may invoke appraisal, each side paying its own appraiser and sharing the umpire; the disputed claim is not settled at the desk.

## Provisions no longer in force

The following earlier provisions are retired and are **no longer in force**; they are kept here only as a record, each with the basis that supersedes it:

1. The former single settlement sequence (actual cash value, less unrepaired prior damage, plus sales tax on that adjusted value, plus the title fee, plus custom equipment up to the limit, less the deductible net of Deductible Rewards credit, less the salvage value for an owner-retained vehicle, each step rounded to the cent) — no longer in force; superseded by the surrender settlement and kept-vehicle settlement bases now in effect.
2. The former new car replacement provision, under which replacement cost new took the place of actual cash value for a vehicle bought new within the age and mileage limits on a package with new car replacement, with no prior damage deducted — no longer in force; superseded by the new car replacement value basis for surrendered vehicles and the actual-cash-value basis for kept vehicles now in effect.
3. The former payoff-difference provision, under which, when the payoff exceeded the settlement and the coverage carried the loan/lease payoff option, the difference was paid to the loss payee up to the benefit cap percentage of actual cash value, excluding the deductible, past-due loan payments, late charges and lease excess-wear or excess-mileage charges — no longer in force; superseded by the loan payoff benefit basis now in effect.

superseded_clauses: The settlement is computed in this order: actual cash value, less unrepaired prior damage where prior_damage_deduction_applies, plus sales tax at the policy_state's rate in sales_tax_rate_by_state on that adjusted value, plus the state's title fee from title_fee_by_state, plus aftermarket custom equipment up to custom_equipment_limit, less the deductible (net of Deductible Rewards credit), less the salvage_value when the customer keeps the vehicle as owner-retained salvage (where owner_retained_salvage_allowed); each step is rounded to the cent.

Where the auto package has new_car_replacement_included true and the vehicle was bought new, is no more than new_car_replacement_max_age_months months past its acquisition date and has no more than new_car_replacement_max_miles miles at the loss, replacement_cost_new replaces actual cash value in the first step and no prior damage is deducted.

When the payoff exceeds the settlement and the coverage carries the loan/lease payoff option, the difference is paid to the loss payee up to loan_lease_payoff_pct_of_acv of actual cash value; the deductible, past-due loan payments, late charges and lease excess-wear or excess-mileage charges are never part of that difference.
